additions.name: Kapahulu Market
additions.note: The Honolulu Zoo unveiled Kapahulu Market, its new food and beverage facility, in late August 2022, replacing the zoo's original 1951 concession.

additions.name: Monkeypod Kitchen
additions.note: Monkeypod Kitchen by Merriman opened on July 14, 2023 at the Outrigger Reef Waikiki Beach Resort, 2169 Kalia Road.

additions.name: La Mer
additions.note: French restaurant at the Halekulani hotel; it opened simultaneously with the rebuilt hotel's grand opening in March 1984. Hawaii's longest-running AAA Five Diamond restaurant, since 1990.

additions.name: Eggs 'n Things
additions.note: Flagship restaurant of the Waikiki breakfast chain; the Saratoga Road restaurant opened March 10, 2009. The brand began on Ena Road in 1974 and the Saratoga site is the third location of the original restaurant. Note: the other Waikiki location, the Waikiki Beach Eggspress at 2464 Kalakaua Ave (opened 2011), was submitted in an earlier run; one travel guide lists this address as 339 Saratoga Road,

additions.name: Heavenly Island Lifestyle
additions.note: All-day restaurant inside Shoreline Hotel Waikiki serving locally sourced island dishes; first welcomed guests in September 2014.

additions.name: Kai Coffee
additions.note: Kai Coffee Hawaii kiosk on the ground floor of Waikiki Shopping Plaza; the plaza's directory listing for it was published in September 2023 and its October 2023 'What's New to Eat' page calls it the brand's newest location.

additions.name: Rivals Waikiki
additions.note: Vegas-inspired sports bar and UltraLounge in the Waikiki Malia Hotel, listed as operating since 2011.

additions.name: Crystal Nail Salon
additions.note: Nail salon in the Waikiki Marketplace at 2310 Kuhio Ave, specializing in manicures and pedicures; established in 2006.

additions.name: Aloha Table Waikiki
additions.note: Hawaiian restaurant best known for its Kobe-style loco moco. It closed on June 25, 2025, after about 16 years, when its lease ran out.

additions.name: Moose McGillycuddy's Pub & Cafe Waikiki
additions.note: Waikiki branch of the Moose McGillycuddy's pub and restaurant chain, opened on Lewers Street in 1980. It was boarded up during the 2020 pandemic and later listed as permanently closed, and Tropics Island Grill & Ale House soft-opened at the address in October 2026.

additions.name: Hyatt Regency Waikiki Farmers Market
additions.note: Indoor farmers market in the Pualeilani Atrium Shops on the Hyatt Regency Waikiki's ground floor, begun in November 2013 as a Thursday evening market. It later moved to other weekday evenings.

additions.name: Starbucks Reserve
additions.note: Starbucks in the former Waikiki Trade Center at Kuhio and Seaside avenues, reportedly open since 2000. In 2017 it added Hawaii's first Starbucks Reserve coffee bar, decorated with island-inspired designs and a mural by a local artist.

additions.name: Morimoto Asia Waikiki
additions.note: Pan-Asian restaurant by Iron Chef Masaharu Morimoto and the signature restaurant of the 'Alohilani Resort Waikiki Beach. It opened to the public on February 15, 2018.

additions.name: Mai Tai Bar
additions.note: Beachfront bar at the Royal Hawaiian Hotel, dated to around 1953, when Trader Vic Bergeron created the hotel's Royal Mai Tai using orange and pineapple juice. Bergeron had invented the original Mai Tai in 1944.

additions.name: Kuhio Beach Hula Mound
additions.note: An open-air hula mound on Kuhio Beach across from the Hyatt Regency, built in the city's first phase of Kuhio Beach improvements. The new beach park was blessed in August 2000 and the mound opened with a concert, and the free Kuhio Beach Hula Show is performed there.

additions.name: KONA Coffee Purveyors
additions.note: Flagship cafe of Kona Coffee Purveyors at International Market Place, which opened with the mall's grand opening in August 2016; the roasting company itself was founded in 2008.

additions.name: Maui Brewing Company
additions.note: Brewpub and restaurant on the second floor of the Waikiki Beachcomber hotel, opened January 31, 2017 as Maui Brewing's first Oahu location.

additions.name: Kai Coffee Hawaii
additions.note: The coffee shop's first location, in the Pualeilani Atrium Shops on the ground floor of the Hyatt Regency Waikiki. It opened on May 15, 2014.

additions.name: Blue Ocean Seafood & Steak
additions.note: Seafood and steak food truck in a converted shipping container at 2449 Kuhio Avenue, in business since 2012.

additions.name: Búho Cocina y Cantina
additions.note: Búho Cocina y Cantina is a rooftop Mexican restaurant and bar atop Waikiki Shopping Plaza, open since 2014.

additions.name: Boardriders
additions.note: 7,000-square-foot flagship surf retail store steps from the Duke Kahanamoku statue; reopened in early 2026 after previous closures.

additions.name: MCM
additions.note: Boutique of the luxury leather goods brand MCM on the first level (Queen's Court) of the International Market Place. It opened around 2019 as part of the brand's U.S. expansion.

additions.name: Michael Kors
additions.note: Michael Kors opened its boutique at the renovated International Market Place (2330 Kalakaua Ave, Suite 186) in Waikiki when the center opened in August 2016.

additions.name: American Wagyu Eatery
additions.note: Giftly reports the eatery opened in June 2022. ALOCO identifies its Waikiki food truck at 2525 Cartwright Rd.

additions.name: Double Fat Ice Cream
additions.note: Hawaii News Now says Double Fat Ice Cream was established in Hawaii in 2021 and located behind the Alohilani Resort. Honolulu Magazine identifies its location as the resort at 124 Kealohilani Ave.

additions.name: Queensbreak Restaurant
additions.note: The resort announced completion of its renovation in August 2021, including the new Queensbreak outdoor restaurant. Queensbreak lists its address as 2552 Kalakaua Ave.

additions.name: Honolulu Cookie Company
additions.note: Shop of the Hawaii-based shortbread cookie maker in the rebuilt International Market Place (Space 162). It opened around the time the center reopened in 2016.

additions.name: Kirin Restaurant
additions.note: HAWAIʻI Magazine's Nov. 29, 2017 article reports Kirin had moved to Hyatt Regency Waikiki and lists 2424 Kalakaua Ave #103. Honolulu Magazine in April 2018 independently describes it reopening at the Hyatt; current restaurant site confirms the address.

additions.name: Edge of Waikiki
additions.note: Oceanfront bar beside the adults-only Infinity Edge Pool at the Sheraton Waikiki, with views toward Diamond Head. The pool and bar were part of a hotel renovation and opened in fall 2009.

additions.name: Honolulu Coffee
additions.note: Kona coffee cafe and kiosk of the Honolulu-based roaster at the Sheraton Waikiki, one poolside and one near the hotel entrance. Both are still open; when they opened isn't known yet.

additions.name: The Cookie Corner
additions.note: Shop in the Sheraton Waikiki lobby run by The Cookie Corner, a Honolulu cookie bakery founded in the early 1980s. It is still open, but when this shop opened has not been confirmed.

additions.name: Royal Hawaiian Bakery
additions.note: The Royal Hawaiian's press release and Honolulu Magazine report the bakery opened February 1, 2017; the release lists the resort address as 2259 Kalakaua Avenue.

additions.name: Izakaya Pau Hana Base
additions.note: Izakaya Pau Hana Base operates at 407 Seaside Ave (#107) in Waikiki and was open by at least 2017.

additions.name: Sushi Sho
additions.note: Honolulu Magazine reported in September 2016 that Sushi Sho had quietly opened at the Ritz-Carlton Residences Waikiki; Travelweek dates its opening to mid-September, and Ritz-Carlton confirms its current address.

additions.name: La Vie
additions.note: French-inspired fine dining restaurant on the lobby level of The Ritz-Carlton Residences, Waikiki Beach, which opened in 2019 in place of BLT Market. It was rebranded as Solera Waikiki in spring 2025.

additions.name: Topped Waikiki
additions.note: Topped Waikiki relocated from Kuhio Ave to 333 Royal Hawaiian Ave (Unit B) in May 2021.

additions.name: Waikiki Market
additions.note: Grocery store on the second floor of the Lilia Waikiki apartment tower, opened on January 11, 2023 on the former site of the Food Pantry store. It closed in spring 2026 for renovation and reopened that August.

additions.name: Sushi Spot Waikiki
additions.note: Sushi restaurant at the corner of Kuhio and Liliʻuokalani avenues, a Waikiki offshoot of the owner's earlier Sushi Spot in Aiea, open by about 2022. In 2025 it began serving brunch in the same space as Brunch Spot Waikiki.

additions.name: Vive Hotel Waikiki
additions.note: Boutique hotel on Kuhio Avenue that opened in mid-2013, with its guest rooms and suites on the upper floors above a parking garage.

additions.name: Genius Lounge Japanese Sake Bar ＆ Dining
additions.note: Genius Lounge Japanese Sake Bar & Dining opened in November 2009 at 346 Lewers St in Waikiki.

additions.name: Skybox Taphouse
additions.note: Skybox Taphouse opened on September 9, 2021 on the 3rd floor Grand Lanai of International Market Place (2330 Kalakaua Ave #302).

additions.name: Mitsuwa Marketplace
additions.note: The Japanese supermarket chain's first Hawaii store, which opened in May 2017 on the second level of International Market Place near Saks Fifth Avenue. Its food court was later remodeled and renamed The Japan.

additions.name: Magnolia Ice Cream & Treats
additions.note: Filipino-inspired ice cream shop on the second level of International Market Place, known for ube ice cream and halo-halo. The chain opened its first Hawaii scoop shop in Waipahu in 2015, and the year this Waikiki shop opened has not been confirmed.

additions.name: Waikiki Shokudo
additions.address: 355 Royal Hawaiian Ave, Suite 201, Honolulu, HI 96815
additions.note: Westman Corporation's history in Aloha State Daily says Waikiki Shokudo opened on Royal Hawaiian Avenue in February 2024; Honolulu Magazine reported on the new restaurant, and its official page confirms the address.

additions.name: Liliha
additions.note: Liliha Bakery opened its Waikiki location on the 3rd floor Grand Lanai of International Market Place (2330 Kalakaua Ave) in November 2021.

additions.name: Honolulu Cookie Company
additions.note: Tabelog lists the Waikiki Beach Walk store at 227 Lewers St and records its opening in 2007; Honolulu Cookie Company's official history says several new Waikiki stores opened that year, and its current locator confirms the address.

additions.name: Penny's Waikiki Malasadas
additions.note: Malasada shop on the second level of Building B at Royal Hawaiian Center, the first storefront of a business that began as a food truck in Lāʻie in 2018. It opened at the center around 2021–2022.

additions.name: Breakout Waikiki
additions.note: Live-action escape room venue at Waikiki Beach Walk. It moved here from its first location at King's Village and held a grand re-opening in May 2019.

additions.name: Honolulu Noodle & Co.
additions.note: Taiwanese beef noodle shop in the STIX ASIA food hall on the lower level of Waikiki Shopping Plaza. It opened in early 2023 as the food hall launched.

additions.name: Nori Bar
additions.note: Aloha State Daily reports Nori Bar just opened its Waikiki location on Kūhiō Avenue in April 2026 and gives the contact address as 2255 Kūhiō Ave. The restaurant’s official site confirms the Waikiki location at that address; the task did not list one.

additions.name: natuRe waikiki
additions.note: natuRe waikiki is a sustainable Island French restaurant that opened December 17, 2021, on the second floor at 413 Seaside Avenue in Waikiki.

additions.name: Waikiki Gun Club
additions.note: The Hawaii Waikiki Gun Club, an indoor shooting range at 2142 Kalakaua Avenue, 2nd Floor, was established in 1988 and remains in operation at that address.

additions.name: Aloha Greek
additions.note: Aloha Greek Waikiki, a self-serve frozen Greek yogurt shop, opened in March 2026 at 2375 Kuhio Ave in Waikiki.

additions.name: Honolulu Skewer House
additions.note: Northern Chinese skewer restaurant that moved here from Makaloa Street, where it opened in 2018. It reopened in Unit 1A in December 2020, with grills at each table so diners cook their own skewers.

additions.name: bb.q Chicken
additions.note: bb.q Chicken opened its third Hawaii location, a Korean fried chicken restaurant, at 2250 Kalakaua Ave, Suite 114, in Waikiki Shopping Plaza in 2025.

additions.name: Aloha Hot Dog & Banh Mi
additions.note: Aloha Hot Dog & Banh Mi, a Vietnamese-Hawaiian fusion stall serving hot dogs on Hawaiian buns and banh mi sandwiches, opened in 2024 on the lower level of Waikiki Shopping Plaza at 2250 Kalakaua Ave, Unit LL105.

additions.name: Waffle and Berry
additions.note: Waffle and Berry, a locally owned waffle and acai bowl cafe established in 2019 at Ohana Hale Marketplace, opened at its current Waikiki Shopping Plaza location, 2250 Kalakaua Ave, Lower Level #104, in 2023.

additions.name: Noa
additions.note: Noa Botanicals (Noa), a medical cannabis dispensary, opened its Waikiki location at 345 Royal Hawaiian Avenue on April 19, 2025.

additions.name: Sam's Kitchen Express
additions.note: Takeout branch of the Waikiki plate-lunch restaurant Sam's Kitchen, known for garlic shrimp, in Waikiki Shopping Plaza. It opened around 2025 and is still open.

additions.name: Allegrini Italian Deli & Market
additions.note: Allegrini Mozzarella, an authentic Italian deli and market, opened at 2250 Kalakaua Ave in the Waikiki Shopping Plaza's lower level at the end of 2024, after previously operating in Downtown Honolulu.

additions.name: Nana's Green Tea
additions.note: Japanese matcha cafe that opened in December 2016 in the Waikiki Yokocho food alley, in the basement of Waikiki Shopping Plaza. It was the chain's first U.S. location. It soft-opened again in the same space in January 2023 as part of the Stix Asia food hall.

additions.name: Shanghai Bar
additions.note: Cocktail bar with a 1930s Shanghai theme in the STIX ASIA food hall on the lower level of Waikiki Shopping Plaza. It was serving Asian-inspired cocktails and Japanese spirits by spring 2023.

additions.name: Haleiwa Town Shave Ice
additions.note: Haleiwa Town Shave Ice opened at the end of 2024 on the basement/lower level of the Waikiki Shopping Plaza at 2250 Kalakaua Ave, bringing North Shore-style shave ice to Waikiki.

additions.name: Udon Yama
additions.note: Udon Yama, a Japanese restaurant serving handmade Sanuki udon, opened in February 2023 as one of the original tenants of the STIX ASIA food hall on the lower level of the Waikiki Shopping Plaza at 2250 Kalakaua Ave.

additions.name: Good Chicken
additions.note: Korean fried chicken stall, a second location of the Kaka'ako shop, that soft-opened in March 2024 in the STIX ASIA food hall on the lower level of Waikiki Shopping Plaza.

additions.name: Tanaka of Tokyo
additions.note: The original Hawaii location of the Tanaka of Tokyo teppanyaki steakhouse, now called Tanaka of Tokyo Central, opened in Waikiki Shopping Plaza in 1978. It reportedly moved from the plaza's fourth floor to its third floor in 2012.

additions.name: Honolulu Cookie Company
additions.note: Company history dates the Waikiki Shopping Plaza store opening to 2020; its store locator identifies this address.

additions.name: Sephora
additions.note: Sephora opened its third Hawaii store, about 7,500 square feet, at Waikiki Shopping Plaza in September 2010.

additions.name: Ribs & Broth
additions.note: Vietnamese pho shop known for beef back rib pho, on the Noodle Street section of the STIX ASIA food hall on the lower level of Waikiki Shopping Plaza. It opened around January 2024.

additions.name: Ramen Baikohken
additions.note: Waikiki branch of a Michelin-listed ramen shop from Asahikawa, Hokkaido. It opened in February 2017 in the Waikiki Yokocho food alley in the basement of Waikiki Shopping Plaza, then reopened in the same space when the STIX Asia food hall launched in 2023.

additions.name: Sushi Matsuri
additions.note: Sushi counter from Japan's Setouchi region serving nigiri and maki in the STIX ASIA food hall on the lower level of Waikiki Shopping Plaza. It was one of the 13 restaurants open at the food hall's grand opening on February 6, 2023.

additions.name: Ao Gelato
additions.note: Gelato shop run by Nana's Green Tea, making gelato with premium teas and tropical fruits. It was one of the original eateries at the February 2023 opening of the STIX ASIA food hall on the lower level of Waikiki Shopping Plaza.

additions.name: Tempura Kiki
additions.note: Japanese tempura restaurant, also called Kiki Authentic Tempura, in the STIX ASIA food hall on the lower level of Waikiki Shopping Plaza. It opened in 2023 in the space formerly held by Tempura Kaneko Hannosuke.

additions.name: Shingen
additions.note: Japanese noodle shop known for fresh soba in the STIX ASIA food hall on the lower level of Waikiki Shopping Plaza. It was one of the restaurants open at the food hall's grand opening in February 2023.

additions.name: Hilton Waikiki Beach
additions.note: The former Prince Kuhio hotel, earlier run by Outrigger and then Radisson, officially became the Hilton Waikiki Prince Kuhio on April 5, 2007 after a $65 million renovation. It later took the Hilton Waikiki Beach name.

additions.name: Hyatt Regency Waikiki Beach Resort and Spa
additions.note: Large beachfront hotel with twin octagonal towers, built in 1976 by developer Chris Hemmeter on the site of the demolished Waikiki Biltmore Hotel. It still operates under the Hyatt Regency name.

additions.name: OUTRIGGER Waikiki Beach Resort
additions.note: Oceanfront Waikiki hotel established in 1967 on land that had been occupied by the Outrigger Canoe Club. It celebrated its 50th anniversary in 2017 and has 524 rooms.

additions.name: Waikiki Resort Hotel
additions.note: Nineteen-story hotel on Koa Avenue, built around 1970 and still operating. It had a major renovation in 2008.

additions.name: Stay Hotel Waikiki
additions.note: Hotel on Koa Avenue in a building that was long a dormitory for University of Hawaiʻi students. It opened as a budget hotel in 2011.

additions.name: Ka Laʻi Waikiki Beach, LXR Hotels & Resorts
additions.note: Luxury condo-hotel on Saratoga Road that joined Hilton's LXR Hotels & Resorts on February 7, 2024. It was previously the Trump International Hotel Waikiki, and its owners bought out the Trump licensing agreement before the rebrand.

additions.name: 'Alohilani Resort Waikiki Beach
additions.note: Oceanfront resort created from the former Pacific Beach Hotel through a $125 million transformation. It celebrated its grand opening on May 8, 2018.

additions.name: Halepuna Waikiki by Halekulani
additions.note: Sister hotel of the Halekulani, across the street from it, created by a year-long renovation of the former Waikiki Parc Hotel. It welcomed its first guests on October 25, 2019, closed during the 2020 pandemic and reopened on April 1, 2021.

additions.name: La Piña Cantina
additions.note: Mexican cantina serving margaritas, tequila and Mexican dishes in the Kūhiō Ave Food Hall on Level 1 of International Market Place. It was one of the hall's first two vendors when the hall opened in spring 2021.

additions.name: Big Island Burger
additions.note: Big Island Burger opened at the end of 2024 in Unit 102 of the Waikiki Shopping Plaza.

additions.name: Secret Spot
additions.note: Secret Spot Honolulu, a café-bar and live-music venue in Space A of The Laylow Waikiki, held its grand opening beginning June 17, 2024.

additions.name: Hyatt Place Waikiki Beach
additions.note: Hawaii's first Hyatt Place, created by renovating and rebranding the former Ocean Resort Hotel Waikiki. Its Pali Tower opened on December 8, 2011, and its Diamond Head Tower followed in April 2012.

additions.name: Waikiki Beach Marriott Resort & Spa
additions.note: Marriott bought the Hawaiian Regent Hotel, which opened in 1971, in November 2000 and renamed it the Waikiki Beach Marriott Resort. A $60 million renovation was finished in early 2002.

additions.name: The Surfjack Hotel & Swim Club
additions.note: Boutique hotel with 112 rooms in a midcentury style, which opened on March 31, 2016, in a renovated Lewers Street building from around 1960. Its pool deck hosts the Swim Club, and Ed Kenney's restaurant Mahina and Sun's is also inside.

additions.name: Shoreline Hotel Waikiki
additions.note: Boutique hotel with 135 rooms on Seaside Avenue, formerly the Seaside Hotel, once owned by United Airlines. It reopened as Shoreline Hotel Waikiki in spring 2013 after a renovation under Joie de Vivre Hotels.

additions.name: OHANA Waikiki Malia
additions.note: Kuhio Avenue hotel renamed from Waikiki Malia to OHANA Waikiki Malia in March 2000, when Outrigger put all its OHANA-brand hotels under that name. Outrigger used the OHANA name until about 2020, and by 2021 the hotel was called Waikiki Malia by Outrigger.

additions.name: The Laylow Waikiki, Autograph Collection
additions.note: Boutique hotel on Kuhio Avenue and Oahu's first Marriott Autograph Collection property. Its grand opening was announced in May 2017 after a renovation.

additions.name: Waikiki Community Center
additions.note: Nonprofit community center founded in 1978 that serves Waikiki seniors and children. It first operated at other Waikiki sites and moved to the former St. Augustine School grounds after the state bought them in 1981.

additions.name: Denny's
additions.note: Hawaii Lodging & Tourism Association's July 2018 archive reports attending the new Denny's grand opening at the Kuhio/Kapahulu intersection; Denny's current location directory confirms 208 Kapahulu Avenue.

additions.name: Aston at the Waikiki Banyan
additions.note: All-suite condominium hotel in the twin-tower Waikiki Banyan, a block from Waikiki Beach, now run by Aston. The towers date from the late 1970s, and the Aston name came later.

additions.name: Harumi Izakaya
additions.address: 339 Royal Hawaiian Avenue, Suite 101, Honolulu, HI 96815
additions.note: A September 2024 roundup of newly opened Hawaii restaurants identifies Harumi Izakaya at 339 Royal Hawaiian Avenue. The restaurant's website confirms Suite 101.

additions.name: Cuckoo Coconuts Waikiki
additions.note: Open-air tiki bar on Royal Hawaiian Avenue between Kalakaua and Kuhio avenues, known for nightly live music and tropical cocktails. A tiki-bar directory dates its opening to about 2014.

additions.name: Wayfinder Waikiki
additions.note: The hotel's site reports an initial opening January 9, 2023. A later announcement places the official grand opening in May 2023 at 2375 Ala Wai Boulevard.

additions.name: Park Shore Waikiki
additions.note: High-rise hotel at the Diamond Head end of Waikiki, across from Kapiolani Park and near the Honolulu Zoo, built around 1968. It still operates as a hotel.

additions.name: Queen Kapiolani Hotel
additions.note: The hotel's own history says it opened in 1969 and gives 150 Kapahulu Avenue as its address.

additions.name: Aston Waikiki Beach Tower
additions.note: All-suite condominium hotel in a tower across from Kuhio Beach, opened around 1984 and later run under the ResortQuest and Aston names. In 2018 it relaunched after a renovation as The Residences at Waikiki Beach Tower.

additions.name: Royal Hawaiian Hotel
additions.note: Beachfront hotel on Kalakaua Avenue that opened on February 1, 1927, according to the Historic Hawai‘i Foundation. It is still operating.

additions.name: Waikiki Circle Hotel
additions.note: Round, 14-story hotel across Kalakaua Avenue from Waikiki Beach, opened around 1962–1963 (the hotel itself gives 1963). It has operated under the Aston and Castle management brands.

additions.name: Hilton Garden Inn Waikiki Beach
additions.note: Hilton Garden Inn hotel on Kuhio Avenue across from International Market Place, opened in June 2016 as the brand's first property on Oahu. It took over and fully renovated the former Ohana Waikiki West hotel.

additions.name: Moana Surfrider
additions.note: Historic Hotels of America identifies this address and the original Moana Hotel opening on March 11, 1901. Moana Surfrider is its current name, so the year refers to the original hotel.

additions.name: Sheraton Waikiki
additions.note: Large beachfront hotel on Kalakaua Avenue that opened on June 4, 1971. After a renovation finished in 2023 it was renamed the Sheraton Waikiki Beach Resort.

additions.name: Wyndham at Waikiki Beach Walk
additions.note: Wyndham timeshare resort with 195 units in two towers, redeveloped from former Ohana hotel buildings during the Waikiki Beach Walk project and opened for guests in November 2006. It now operates as Club Wyndham at Waikiki Beach Walk.

additions.name: Aloha Surf Hotel
additions.note: Condo-hotel on Kanekapolei Street in a 15-story building completed around 1968. It still operates today as Aqua Aloha Surf Waikiki.

additions.name: Romer House Waikiki
additions.note: Adults-only hotel that opened June 1, 2024 after a $29 million renovation of a 1960 building, first built as the Royal Prince Apartment Building and later known as the Pearl Hotel. It was billed as Oahu's first adults-only hotel.

additions.name: Waikiki Grand Hotel
additions.note: Hotel across from the Honolulu Zoo, built around 1962–63 by developer Kanae Kobayashi to a design by architect Ernest Hara. It opened with 172 rooms at $7.50 to $24 a night and still operates as a condo-hotel.

additions.name: Ilima Hotel
additions.note: Family-owned condo-style hotel with 98 rooms on Nohonani Street, open since 1968 and still operating.

additions.name: Hotel Renew
additions.note: Boutique hotel with 72 rooms near the Diamond Head end of Waikiki. It opened in 2008 after a multimillion-dollar remodel of an older building, formerly the Ocean Tower Hotel, and Aston Hotels & Resorts took over running it in 2013.

additions.name: Hokulani Waikiki by Hilton Grand Vacations
additions.note: Hilton Grand Vacations timeshare resort at Kalakaua Avenue and Lewers Street, built in place of the former OHANA Islander Waikiki Hotel. It opened in December 2013 and held its grand opening in January 2014.

fields.note: A 750-seat theater on the fourth floor of Royal Hawaiian Center, opened around July 2008 as Level 4 for the Waikiki Nei show. Today it is the Royal Hawaiian Theater, home of the Rock-A-Hula show.
Opened at Royal Hawaiian Center in March 2008. It reopened in September 2021 after a major renovation.
Lingerie and clothing store at the corner of Kalākaua and Royal Hawaiian avenues. It held its grand opening on October 11, 2011, with model Alessandra Ambrosio, and is still open.
Open-air restaurant and bar on the second floor of the Park Shore Waikiki hotel at Kalākaua and Kapahulu. It opened in November 2004 in the space Denny's had left earlier that year.
Bar and lounge that opened in August 2011 on the second floor of Royal Hawaiian Center, near the Paina Lanai food court, replacing the former Grove Bar. Still open today.

fields.name: Eggs 'n Things Waikiki Beach Eggspress
fields.note: A quick-service and takeout branch of the Waikiki breakfast chain, which started on Ena Road in 1974. It opened in late 2011 in the lobby of the Waikiki Circle Hotel.

Brewpub that opened in 2015 at the corner of Kalakaua Ave and Ala Moana Blvd, Waikiki's first brewery. The company later moved its main brewing to Kakaako, and the Waikiki pub reopened after a full renovation in November 2020.
Opened around 2007 as the 24-hour signature restaurant of the Hilton Waikiki Prince Kuhio, after the hotel's $65 million renovation and switch to Hilton. The hotel is now Hilton Waikiki Beach.
Tiki bar in the Ohia Waikiki Studio Suites building, renamed from Lava Tube around May 2025. It closed in April 2026 when its lease ended ahead of renovations.
Opened in December 2016 inside the Hilton Garden Inn Waikiki Beach, as the chain's second restaurant and first franchise location. It took over the hotel's former Chili's space.
Self-serve udon restaurant that opened April 1, 2011 as Marukame Udon, the Japanese chain's first Hawaii location. It later took the name Marugame Udon.

Bank of Hawaii moved its Waikiki branch to the ground floor of this building, renamed the Bank of Hawaii Waikiki Center, around mid-2008. The branch had been at Kalakaua and Royal Hawaiian, and the ground-floor space was formerly the Wyland Gallery.
Second-floor gay bar on Lewers Street at Kuhio Avenue. It held its grand opening party in August 2011.
Hawaii gift and beach-decor shop in the International Market Place, among the retailers when the rebuilt mall opened on August 25, 2016.
Oceanfront restaurant at the Halekulani hotel. It likely opened with the rebuilt hotel in 1984, though no exact opening date has been found.
A 17-story hotel with about 250 rooms on Kuhio Avenue. It was formerly the Outrigger Surf East and took the Ohia Waikiki name in June 2015, when Aqua Hospitality took over and refurbished it.
Café, market and beer-and-wine bar inside the Hilton Garden Inn Waikiki Beach, run by Food Pantry, Ltd. (Foodland's parent company). It opened with the hotel in mid-2016.

Opened December 10, 2003 as an anchor restaurant at the Royal Hawaiian Shopping Center, the chain's first Hawaii location. It closed briefly after a kitchen fire in February 2013 and is still open today.

Open-air beachfront restaurant and bar in the Outrigger Waikiki Beach Resort, named for surfer Duke Kahanamoku. TS Restaurants opened it in 1992 as the second Duke's, after the 1989 original on Kauai.
Burger restaurant on Kalakaua Avenue that opened in 1997 as the Waikiki branch of a Lahaina restaurant founded in 1989.

Live music club in the Outrigger Waikiki Beach Resort, in the former Society of Seven showroom. Blue Note Entertainment Group held its grand opening in January 2016 after soft-opening shows from late December 2015.
Pizza shop that moved to Seaside Avenue in November 2024. It had sold pizza from a small window on Kuhio Avenue since 2011.
Central Pacific Bank's Waikiki Branch, a street-level bank branch on Seaside Avenue. FDIC records date the branch office to September 1979.
Build-your-own poke shop on Seaside Avenue, near Ross Dress for Less. It opened in April 2023.
Nail salon at 2229 Kuhio Ave. Its owner applied for a state beauty shop license in late 2013, and the salon is still open.
Oceanfront restaurant run by TS Restaurants on the second floor of the Outrigger Waikiki Beach Resort, above Duke's Waikiki. It opened in mid-2004, with dinner service planned to start June 22.
Oceanfront restaurant and rum bar on the ground floor of the Sheraton Waikiki, opened in early 2008. It was later remodeled and is still open.
Dean & DeLuca's first Hawaii store opened here in the Ritz-Carlton Residences Waikiki on September 14, 2016. It has a cafe and market downstairs and a wine lounge upstairs.
Local burger chain founded in 1998 on Monsarrat Avenue. It moved here to the Waikiki Grand hotel, into a former Jack in the Box space, in July 2004.

fields.name: Da Big Kahuna
fields.note: Tiki bar and restaurant in the hotel building at 2280 Kuhio Ave, known for its fish bowl cocktail. It became Lava Tube in 2018 and later Tiki's Meeting Spot, which closed in April 2026.
Casual bar and grill on Kuhio Avenue known for cheap breakfasts. Travel listings from 2006 said it had been around since 1996, and it is still open.

Indoor shooting range for visitors, open today on the 3rd floor at 339 Royal Hawaiian Ave. A gun club of this name earlier operated for many years at 2266 Kuhio Ave until about 2017; the year it opened here is not known.
Poke shop that serves bowls made with local ahi. It opened in Waikiki on December 31, 2021.
Tapa's Waikiki, an independent LGBTQ+ bar and restaurant up one flight at 407 Seaside Ave, has been open since about 2003. It is known for karaoke, monthly drag shows and a free pool table.
Japanese okonomiyaki and teppanyaki restaurant on the ground floor of the Pacific Monarch Hotel, open since September 2008. It is a branch of a Tokyo restaurant founded in 1989.

Iron Chef Masaharu Morimoto's casual ramen and sake restaurant on the ground floor of the 'Alohilani Resort, across from Kuhio Beach. It opened in May 2018, three months after his Morimoto Asia Waikiki opened one floor above.
Matcha cafe serving soft serve, parfaits and lattes made with matcha from Kyoto's Harima Garden. It opened in July 2016 in the Kuhio Banyan building.
Hawaiian-Cajun seafood boil restaurant on an upper floor of International Market Place, open there by late 2022. It reopened in October 2024 after a brief Health Department closure.
Budget apartment-style hotel and timeshare in central Waikiki, across from the International Market Place. Travel listings say it opened around 1960 and was renovated in 2015.
Thai restaurant on the second floor of a small building at Lewers Street and Kuhio Avenue. A local newspaper reviewed it in 2008, and listings say it has been open since about 1999.

Northern Italian restaurant on the lobby level of The Wyland Waikiki, which opened in 2008 and stayed on after the hotel became the Courtyard by Marriott Waikiki Beach. It had closed by 2021, when KALO: Hawaiian Food by Chai's opened in its space.
Neapolitan-style pizza and wine bar on the ground floor of the Ohana East hotel, in the former Keoni by Keo's space. It opened in fall 2017 and held its grand opening in January 2018.
Retro South Pacific-style tiki restaurant and bar upstairs in the Aston Waikiki Beach Hotel, now the Twin Fin Hotel. It opened in October 2002 and is still open.

Bills was the first U.S. restaurant of Australian chef Bill Granger, opened on the second floor of 280 Beach Walk in March 2014. It closed around 2020, and the space later held Westman Café and then Side Street Inn (opened 2026).

fields.name: Arancino on Beachwalk
fields.note: The original Arancino Italian restaurant, opened on Beach Walk around 1996 by a family who took over an existing Italian restaurant there. Its sister restaurant, Arancino di Mare, opened on Kalākaua Avenue in 2004.
Hard Rock Cafe Honolulu moved from its 1987 site at Kalakaua Avenue and Kapiolani Boulevard to 280 Beach Walk, at the corner of Kalakaua Avenue, in November 2010. It is still open.

Small tiki-style dive bar on Saratoga Road across from the Waikiki Post Office, said to have opened around 1992 in a building that was once a horse stable. It was reviewed in the local press in 2002 and is still open.

Tommy Bahama's three-level Waikiki flagship opened October 30, 2015, with a ground-floor store, a second-floor restaurant and a rooftop lounge. It took over a building that previously housed Burberry and Hawaiian Island Creations.

Longs Drugs, owned by CVS, opened its first Waikiki store here in October 2015. The two-story store with a pharmacy is in the Bank of Hawaii Waikiki Center, in space formerly occupied by Teddy Bear World.
Two-level off-price department store in the former Waikiki Trade Center building, now the Hyatt Centric Waikiki Beach. It opened in spring 2016 and closed permanently on July 27, 2026.
Quick-service Wolfgang Puck Express at the Aston Waikiki Beach Hotel, now the Twin Fin Hotel. It opened in December 2002 as the chain's second Hawaii location and is still open.
Irish pub on Lewers Street known for nightly live music, reported to have operated since about 1994 and mentioned in the local press by 2005.

fields.name: Tucker & Bevvy Picnic Food
fields.note: Australian-style takeout picnic cafe that opened in fall 2013 in the Park Shore Waikiki hotel. It closed on April 1, 2026, and an açaí shop took over the space.
Teppanyaki restaurant (Tanaka of Tokyo East) on the ground floor of the OHANA Waikiki East hotel. It opened in fall 2015 in the former Round Table Pizza space after moving from King's Village.
Waikiki branch of Tonkatsu Ginza Bairin, a tonkatsu restaurant founded in Tokyo's Ginza district in 1927. It opened on Beach Walk in 2007 and is described as the chain's first location outside Asia.
Dry-aged prime steakhouse from Wolfgang Zwiener, a New York steakhouse brand, that opened in February 2009 on the third floor of Royal Hawaiian Center. Still open today.

An open-air shopping and dining center on Helumoa land next to the Royal Hawaiian hotel. It opened around 1979–1980 as the Royal Hawaiian Shopping Center and was rebuilt in a major renovation from 2005 to 2008.
Chef Ed Kenney's island-cuisine restaurant in the Surfjack Hotel & Swim Club, opened in spring 2016. It was his first restaurant in Waikiki.
Tokyo sushi chef Keiji Nakazawa opened this Edomae omakase counter in the Ritz-Carlton Residences Waikiki in September 2016. It was his first restaurant outside Japan.
Locally owned open-air beach bar and grill on Koa Avenue, open since about 2018; it was the original location before a second ShoreFyre opened at the International Market Place around 2020.
Sicilian restaurant on Lewers Street that opened in fall 2007 and is still serving Southern Italian food.
Restaurant and beer hall that opened in February 2007 as one of the first restaurants at the new Waikiki Beach Walk complex. It is still open.

Tesla showroom and gallery in International Market Place's Banyan Court, opened around 2016–2017 after the mall was rebuilt. It closed briefly in March 2019 when Tesla moved sales online, then reopened about a week later.
Modern Japanese teppan and sushi restaurant from Tokyo that opened on the second level of Waikiki Beach Walk around 2007. It is still open.
Spam musubi cafe on the ground floor of the Pacific Monarch Hotel, which moved here from Koa Avenue in July 2014. The Iyasume chain was founded in Waikiki in 2000 in the Waikiki Sand Villa Hotel.
Nail salon at the Waikiki Beach Walk shopping center that opened around 2014–2015, offering Japanese-style nail art along with waxing and lash services. It is still open.
Ukulele shop that opened its first store at Waikiki Beach Walk in May 2016, offering free daily beginner lessons.
Women's fashion boutique selling clothing, swimwear and jewelry with a mix of Hawaiian and French styles, on the ground level of Waikiki Beach Walk. It opened around 2019 and is still open.

The beachfront Royal Hawaiian Hotel, known as the Pink Palace of the Pacific, opened on February 1, 1927. The U.S. military used it as a rest and recreation center during World War II, and it closed for renovation from June 2008 to January 2009.
ABC Stores' upscale market and food hall on the ground floor of the Hyatt Centric Waikiki Beach, the former Waikiki Trade Center, at Kuhio Avenue and Dukes Lane. It opened on July 5, 2017.
Italian restaurant in the Waikiki Beach Marriott Resort & Spa, opened in 2004 as a sister to the original Arancino on Beach Walk. It is still open today.
New York-style deli, pizzeria and sports bar that opened at Waikiki Beach Walk around 2007, soon after the complex's first tenants. Still open today.

fields.name: The Veranda at the Beachhouse
fields.note: Oceanfront veranda dining area, known for afternoon tea, at the Beachhouse restaurant in the Moana Surfrider hotel (opened 1901). The Beachhouse concept began around 2007, when the hotel became a Westin resort.
Japanese-style izakaya and bar in the lobby of the Romer House Waikiki hotel, opened in June 2024 by Table One Hospitality. It is named for the 1-855-ALOHA number of Waikīkī's old sky-blue payphones.

Wine bar with self-serve wine dispensers on the second level of Royal Hawaiian Center's Building C, run by the owner of the Island Vintage Coffee cafe next door. It held its grand opening on August 8, 2019, and is still open today.
Longtime LGBTQ+ bar that opened in 1974 on Kuhio Avenue. After losing its lease there, it moved to the second floor of the Waikiki Grand Hotel around 1998, with views of Diamond Head.

fields.name: Tommy Bahama Restaurant and Bar
fields.note: Tommy Bahama's restaurant and bar opened October 30, 2015, on the second floor of the brand's three-level Waikiki flagship, which also has a ground-floor store and a rooftop lounge.

Ramen Bario opened in 2017 at Waikiki Yokocho, the Japanese food alley in the basement of Waikiki Shopping Plaza. After a stint at Ala Moana, it later reopened in its old space, now part of the STIX Asia food hall.
Poolside tiki bar and restaurant at the Aqua Bamboo Waikiki hotel, which replaced an earlier pizza restaurant on the site. Tourism listings described it as newly opened in early 2020.

House of Mana Up, Mana Up's first store, opened on the ground level of Building A at Royal Hawaiian Center in January 2020. It sells products made by Hawaii businesses in Mana Up's accelerator program, and a newer store opened on the center's ground floor in early 2026.
French-Japanese fine-dining restaurant inside the Espacio hotel. It opened in fall 2019, around the same time as the hotel.

Kona coffee cafe on the second floor of Royal Hawaiian Center, run by a brand that dates its start to 1996. This cafe was built in the newly renovated center and won a remodeling award in 2009, so it likely opened around 2008. Still open today.

Australian skincare and cosmetics shop in Space 116 of International Market Place, opened in 2016 when the rebuilt mall reopened. Its interior uses reclaimed Douglas fir from a 1950s building on Ford Island.
NightRider Jewelry's first Hawaii boutique, in the Banyan Court of International Market Place. It opened in early 2018 and held its official blessing and grand opening on November 17, 2018.
Boutique of the TUMI luggage and travel-goods brand in International Market Place (Suite 112), listed in mall directories by early 2023. It may have opened earlier.
Boutique of the Vince men's and women's clothing brand at International Market Place. It opened around 2017, among the later arrivals after the rebuilt mall reopened in August 2016.
Vans footwear and apparel store in Space 179 of International Market Place, open there by early 2020.

fields.address: Kealohilani Ave (behind ʻAlohilani Resort, 2490 Kalakaua Ave)
fields.note: Italian food truck that opened in late February 2021 on Kealohilani Avenue, behind the ʻAlohilani Resort, according to HAWAIʻI Magazine and Honolulu Magazine.
Kai Coffee Hawaii's third location, a street-facing cafe in the 'Alohilani Resort Waikiki Beach. A June 2019 trade-press report said it had opened that spring.
Poolside restaurant and bar beside the infinity pool on the fifth floor of the 'Alohilani Resort Waikiki Beach. It was open by May 8, 2018, when the resort held its grand opening celebration there.
Buffet restaurant in the Waikiki Beach Marriott Resort & Spa. It was serving Hawaiian dinner buffets by April 2011 and is still open.

Sushi and seafood restaurant on the third floor of the Waikiki Beach Marriott Resort & Spa. It moved there from Restaurant Row around fall 2004, into the former Third Floor and Acqua restaurant space.
Steakhouse from chef D.K. Kodama on the third floor of the Waikiki Beach Marriott Resort & Spa, next to Sansei. It opened in fall 2004, took the d.k Steak House name that December and is still open.
Seafood and steak restaurant on the third floor of the Hyatt Regency Waikiki Beach Resort and Spa. Its grand opening was on June 6, 2011.

Poolside restaurant and bar on the third-floor pool deck of the Hyatt Regency Waikiki Beach Resort & Spa. It opened around 2011 as part of the hotel's third-floor renovation and serves American and local Hawaiian food.
Second location of the Australian-style picnic cafe, in the Pualeilani Atrium Shops on the Hyatt Regency Waikiki's ground floor. It was announced in June 2017 to open that October.
Buffet restaurant featuring locally grown food at the Sheraton Waikiki, opened in August 2009. It is still open.
Pizza and pasta restaurant in the Sheraton Waikiki facing the Infinity Pool, opened around 2014 in a former market space. Its pizzas mix Italian ingredients with Hawaiian flavors.
Ice cream shop in the Sheraton Waikiki that had moved there from the Royal Hawaiian Center by early 2010. The brand still lists it at this address.
Oceanfront restaurant at The Royal Hawaiian hotel, opened in March 2009 after the hotel's renovation, according to the hotel owner Kyo-ya.

Open-air oceanfront restaurant at The Royal Hawaiian, created from the hotel's former Surf Room during its 2008–2009 renovation and opened when the hotel reopened in 2009. It now serves breakfast overlooking Waikiki Beach.

Cafe on the second floor of the OHANA Waikiki East hotel (now Outrigger Waikiki Paradise), in the former Kimo Bean space, reached by a stairway from Kaiulani Avenue. It was scheduled to open in December 2017 and is still open.

Restaurant serving Italian and Mediterranean food with Hawaiian ingredients, in the Diamond Head Tower of The Ritz-Carlton Residences, Waikiki Beach. Local press reported it opened around the end of August 2019.
Convenience store and deli on Ala Wai Boulevard in Waikiki, still open. Business listings give its opening year as about 1969.
Korean soft tofu stew restaurant that opened in late January 2019 at 2299 Kuhio Ave, on the ground floor of The Laylow hotel. It is listed as open today.
Restaurant and bar serving modern Hawaiian food at The Laylow hotel, 2299 Kuhio Ave. It opened in spring 2017 when the hotel opened and is still open today.

Waikiki branch of a family-owned Greek and Mediterranean restaurant that also has other Honolulu locations, in an outdoor food-stall area at 2239 Waikolu Way. It is open today, but the year it opened hasn't been confirmed.
Indian take-out counter in the Royal Hawaiian Dining Plaza food-stall area, known for butter chicken and vegan dishes. It was operating in 2024 and is now listed as closed.
Poke and seafood shop Maguro Brothers moved its Waikiki location to the basement level of Waikiki Shopping Plaza in September 2023.
Lobster roll shop on the lower level of Waikiki Shopping Plaza. Honolulu Magazine described it as a new stand in October 2021.

Halekulani's first branded bakery and restaurant opened in October 2019 with the Halepuna Waikiki hotel (formerly the Waikiki Parc), on the ground floor where Nobu Waikiki used to be. It closed for part of the COVID-19 pandemic and later reopened.
Japanese restaurant on the ground floor of the Park Shore Waikiki hotel, serving sushi, sashimi and sukiyaki. It was established in 1982 and is still open.
Open-air restaurant and bar on the third-floor deck of the Queen Kapiolani Hotel, overlooking Diamond Head and Kapiolani Park. It opened in October 2018 as part of the hotel's $35 million renovation.
Starbucks Café inside the Target store at International Market Place, which opened in late October 2024.

This high-rise went up in the mid-to-late 1960s on the site of the former Coconut Grove Hotel, and it became the Imperial Hawaii Hotel after the Denny's chain bought it in the late 1960s. It added a vacation ownership club in 1980 and still operates as both a hotel and a timeshare.
ABC Stores No. 206 applied for a liquor license at the Outrigger Reef Waikiki Beach Resort in April 2023 and opened around mid-2023. It is a convenience store that is still open.
Shop selling sherbet and shave ice inside Kings & Queens at the Hyatt Regency Waikīkī, across from the Duke Kahanamoku statue, in the former Dylan's Candy Bar space. It opened on November 23, 2025.
A Hawaii chocolate maker's Waikiki shop at Waikiki Beach Walk, which opened as a pop-up in December 2024. The company's site lists it as its current Waikiki store.

Locally owned clothing and beach gear shop on the ground floor of the Hyatt Regency Waikīkī, in the former Dylan's Candy Bar space. It soft-opened in November 2025 and held its grand opening that December.

A matcha drink shop that opened in November 2022 on the ground floor of Royal Hawaiian Center's Building C, Junbi's first Hawaii location. In late 2026 the company's website listed the Waikiki shop as moving soon.

Dean & DeLuca's second Hawaii store, a grab-and-go shop, opened in November 2017 on the first floor of Building B at Royal Hawaiian Center, in the space Royal Fish had left. It sells takeout food and merchandise sold only in Hawaii.

TsuruTonTan Udon Noodle Brasserie, a restaurant from the Japanese udon chain, opened on June 14, 2018, on the third level of Building B at Royal Hawaiian Center. It was the chain's first Hawaii location.
Crystal and gift shop that opened its fourth location at Waikiki Beach Walk in mid-2024. It is still listed among the center's current shops.

Rice ball (musubi) shop using organic Japanese rice in the basement of Waikiki Shopping Plaza. It opened around 2016 as Shichi Musubi in the Waikīkī Yokocho food hall, closed with the hall in 2020, and reopened as Nana Musubi in the Stix Asia food hall in January 2023.

A burger restaurant serving Hawaii-raised grass-fed beef, founded in 2010 by a Honolulu-born chef in the Pāʻina Lānai food court on the second floor of Royal Hawaiian Center. It is the chain's original location.
Asian food hall on the lower level of Waikiki Shopping Plaza, in the space of the former Waikiki Yokocho food hall. It soft-opened in December 2022 and held its grand opening on February 6, 2023.
French underwear, swimwear and apparel brand whose Waikiki Beach Walk shop opened in December 2013. It is still open.
Gelato shop at Waikiki Beach Walk that opened on February 26, 2024, as the local Il Gelato chain's seventh Oahu location. It is still open.
Resort-wear boutique that was on Lewers Street before the redevelopment and was one of the old retailers to return when Waikiki Beach Walk opened around 2007. It is still open.
Flagship store of a Hawaii handcrafted jewelry brand, which opened at Waikiki Beach Walk in 2021. Kolohe's store page still lists it as open.
A branch of the Hong Kong dim sum chain known for its Michelin star, it opened at Royal Hawaiian Center in April 2018 in Building B. Around late 2024 it moved to Level 3 of the center's Building A.
Japanese convenience store in the Sheraton Waikiki that opened in July 2012 as one of Lawson's first two U.S. stores. It is still open.

fields.name: Hyatt Centric Waikiki Beach
fields.note: Hotel in the former Waikīkī Trade Center building, which opened to guests on December 8, 2016. It is still operating.
Poolside restaurant with live Hawaiian music at the Outrigger Reef Waikiki Beach Resort, opened in March 2009 and still open.
Steakhouse on the ground floor of the Lilia Waikiki tower, opened on September 10, 2025 as the chain's first Hawaii location. It is still open.

Smoothie bowl and coffee shack at the entrance of the Outrigger Waikiki Beach Resort, opened in July 2018 as the second location of the North Shore surfer-founded cafe. In late 2026 it was temporarily closed for renovation, with reopening planned for early 2027.
Hidden speakeasy-style cocktail bar inside the White Sands Hotel, opened in March 2023. Guests reach it by asking at the front desk for Room 8.
Waikiki cafe pairing Honolulu Coffee's Kona coffee with mochi donuts and malasadas. A 2026 dessert guide says it opened that year, and it is still open.
Smoothie bowl and coffee shack on the ground floor of the Twin Fin Hotel, across from Kuhio Beach. It held its grand opening in late November 2024 and is still open.
Japanese yakiniku restaurant serving A5 wagyu on the ground floor of the Lilia Waikiki tower. It opened on December 13, 2024 as the second Hawaii location of the Honolulu restaurant.
Donut shop that opened in 2021 as the chain's third Oahu location, after Kaimuki and Kailua. It took over the former 88 Tees space in the Waikiki Marketplace and is still open.

fields.name: Kamukura Surf + Dine
fields.note: Japanese ramen and dining restaurant in the Lilia Waikiki tower, opened in summer 2024 by the Osaka-based Kamukura Ramen group as its first U.S. flagship. It is still open.
Small coffee shop on Kaʻiulani Avenue that announced it was officially open in May 2026. It serves espresso drinks made with beans from an Oahu roaster.

Cafe serving 100% Kona coffee and pastries baked on site, on the ground floor of the Lilia Waikiki tower. It soft-opened in June 2026 and held its grand opening on July 1, 2026, after its original Ka'a'awa cafe closed.

Casual plate-lunch restaurant known for garlic shrimp, which moved from Royal Hawaiian Avenue to the poolside terrace of the Bamboo Waikiki hotel sometime between late 2023 and 2025. It is still open there.
Açaí bowl and smoothie shop on Kūhiō Avenue, open by October 2024 when a social media post described it as newly opened. Still listed as open in OpenStreetMap.
Beef katsu restaurant from Kyoto, Japan, where the chain has four shops. It opened its first U.S. location in late August 2025 in the Stix Asia food hall on the lower level of Waikīkī Shopping Plaza.

Tenōre, the apparel and lifestyle brand founded by Pat Tenore after he left RVCA, opened its first flagship store in Waikiki Shopping Plaza in September 2025. The 12,000-square-foot, two-story store has apparel on the ground floor and a studio for wellness classes and community events upstairs.
Day spa offering massage and other treatments that opened in late 2024 inside the Hilton Waikiki Beach Resort & Spa.
Louis Vuitton's largest Hawaii boutique, in the 1929 Gump Building, a historic landmark. The company bought the building in 1991 and opened the store in October 1992 after restoring it.

Japanese sushi restaurant from Kevin Aoki, son of Benihana founder Rocky Aoki, that opened around the start of 2008 on the third floor of Royal Hawaiian Center. It was renovated in 2019 and in late 2026 was closed for another renovation, with reopening planned for December 2026.
Ice cream shop on Kūhiō Avenue in Waikiki. Its Better Business Bureau profile lists the business as starting in March 2026.

fields.name: La Pure Waikiki Spa & Cafe
fields.note: Day spa with a cafe offering nails, facials and massages on the ground floor of the Lilia Waikiki tower, with its entrance on Walina Street. It opened in September 2025 and is still open.
Vegan cafe serving plant-based light meals and baked goods at 159 Kaʻiulani Ave #105, with its doors on Kūhiō Avenue. It opened in Waikiki in 2021 and later added locations Downtown and in Kakaʻako.
Surf and beach gear rental shop at the Twin Fin Hotel, renting surfboards, paddleboards, chairs and umbrellas. It was operating by the hotel's grand opening in November 2022 and is still open.

Shave ice shop on the ground level of the Twin Fin Hotel, serving chef-designed and savory shave ice. It soft-opened in January 2026, later added a speakeasy cocktail lounge behind the shop, and is still open.

Italian luxury fashion house at Royal Hawaiian Center, first in Building A and from about 2017 in a two-level boutique in Building C. In 2024 it closed its Ala Moana store and opened a larger 3,186 sq ft boutique here, which is still open today.

Beachfront concession in the Kūhiō Beach Park pavilion across from the ʻAlohilani Resort, with a soft opening on June 20, 2022. It began with sunrise breakfasts and Hawaiian storytelling, and it now rents beach loungers and chairs.
Dinner buffet at the Hyatt Regency Waikiki Beach Resort and Spa that opened around February 2018 under a new executive chef. It closed for a time and returned in mid-2023.
Small all-suite luxury boutique hotel, also called ESPACIO The Jewel of Waikiki, that opened in fall 2019. It houses the Mugen restaurant.

Matson opened the Princess Kaiulani Hotel in June 1955 on part of the former ʻĀinahau estate, and at 11 stories it was then Hawaii's tallest building. Sheraton later took it over, and the 29-story ʻĀinahau Tower was added in 1970.
Shop and gallery selling cannabis-themed art and accessories by local artists, next to Noa Botanicals. It opened in August 2025 and also helps customers get Hawaii 329 medical cannabis cards.

Waikiki branch of the Maui-founded Ululani's Hawaiian Shave Ice, in the former Jamba Juice space on Seaside Avenue near the Hyatt Centric. It had its grand opening on October 4, 2025, as the chain's 15th location and fourth on O'ahu.

Restaurant serving contemporary island cuisine inside Waikiki Market, on the second floor of the Lilia Waikiki tower. It opened in 2023, closed with the market in spring 2026 for renovation, and reopened on August 25, 2026.

Juliet and Clifford Kimball bought a hotel on this site and named it the Halekulani in 1917. Mitsui Fudosan bought it in 1981 and rebuilt it, keeping the historic Main Building, and the current hotel had its grand opening in 1984.

Formerly the OHANA Waikiki East, this hotel reopened under the new name on October 16, 2024, Princess Kaʻiulani's birthday, after a renovation of its 443 rooms. Its name comes from Paradise Garden, the old name of the princess's ʻĀinahau estate, which once covered this site.

corrections.target: St. Augustine By the Sea Catholic Church

fields.note: Catholic parish founded in 1854 with a beach chapel, later moved to land on Ohua Avenue, where a permanent church was blessed in 1901. The present modernist church replaced it in 1962.
Family-run museum of rocks, minerals and coral, named for the owners' family name Lu. Sources say it opened around 1989–1990 and it is still open.
Italian restaurant on Royal Hawaiian Avenue that opened in early 2022, listed among Waikiki's February 2022 restaurant openings. It is still operating.

Surf-themed hotel at Kalakaua and Paoakalani avenues, across from Kuhio Beach, run by Highgate. It opened on November 1, 2022, after a renovation of the former Aston Waikiki Beach Hotel, and is still open.
